items.text: What the economy produces should be decided mainly by a deliberate plan rather than by prices and competition.
items.rationale: Core planner claim (production). 'Profit' replaced to avoid ownership bleed; mirrors pla-02.

items.text: Prices and competition alone should decide what gets produced and in what amounts.
items.rationale: New Market production item for sub-facet parity with pla-01; market socialists and liberals both endorse; ownership-neutral.

items.text: Investment in key industries should be steered toward goals set for the whole society, even when it would earn more elsewhere.
items.rationale: Directed investment (industrial policy); 'publicly chosen' dropped to avoid Democratic-axis bleed. Mirrors pla-04.

items.text: Investment in industry should go wherever it is expected to earn the best returns, rather than toward goals chosen by planners.
items.rationale: Return-driven investment; scoped to industry so public budgets are excluded. Mirrors pla-03.

items.text: If the price of a basic necessity such as medicine soars, it should be capped.
items.rationale: Price controls under a plan-favouring condition; single example avoids double cue and housing overlap. Likely frame split.

items.text: If price caps lead to shortages, prices should be left to buyers and sellers.
items.rationale: Market-favouring condition mirroring pla-05; built-in economics justification removed for symmetry.

items.text: If competing firms waste resources duplicating each other's products, production in that industry should be coordinated by a plan.
items.rationale: Competitive-waste critique in planners' terms; 'single plan' dropped to avoid Centralised load. Pairs with pla-08.

items.text: Businesses that lose out to competitors should close rather than be rescued, even large ones that many jobs depend on.
items.rationale: Competitive exit vs rescue; 'rather than be rescued' makes it polar. Plausible frame split.

items.text: Major networks such as power grids and railways should follow a long-term plan rather than the choices of competing providers.
items.rationale: Infrastructure investment; contrasted with competition so market liberals disagree. 'One coordinated' dropped (Centralised load).

items.text: If industries picked out for support keep failing, investment decisions should be left to competing investors.
items.rationale: Market-favouring condition (failed industrial policy); 'officials' bets' softened to neutral tone. Pairs with pla-09.

items.text: Pay and conditions agreed between unions and employers in an industry should apply to every firm in that industry.
items.rationale: Sectoral bargaining (review C3): social partnership coordinates wages outside the market, the Planned pole. Mirrors pla-12. Content v2 separator (CF review 2026-10-31 §5 draft, reworded); original.

items.text: Workers should be free to take a job on terms they agree individually, without any union deal applying to them.
items.rationale: Individual contracting, the Market pole. Mirrors pla-11. Content v2 separator (CF review 2026-10-31 §5 draft, reworded); original.

items.text: A society should improve through many small changes that can be undone if they fail, rather than one complete redesign.
items.rationale: Piecemeal social engineering (Popper) and evolved order (Hayek) against utopian blueprints, so the Market pole; review P4. Content v2 separator (CF review 2026-10-31 §5 draft, reworded); original.

items.text: A deeply unjust society should be rebuilt from the ground up according to a clear plan.
items.rationale: Holistic redesign to a plan, the Planned pole. Mirrors pla-13. Content v2 separator (CF review 2026-10-31 §5 draft, reworded); original.
